clue.text: Force a move to be made by substitute

parts.note: to force someone to do something is to make them do it
a shift is a move or change of position

explanation.surface: A chess-like order: some forced move has to be made by a stand-in player.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift is a temporary stand-in used when the proper thing is unavailable.

clue.text: Book ofthe year

definitions.meaning: a yearly publication, such as a children's ..., is a book

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a yearly publication and anything recurring yearly.

clue.text: Times editor removed the writ ten evidence

parts.note: eras are ages or periods of time

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor at The Times destroys incriminating documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it simply means periods of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has had its writing rubbed out has been wiped clean, deleted.

clue.text: Certainly not a cold vessel for stew

parts.note: the opposite of cold is hot
a pot is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: A warm cooking pot is wanted for making a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: A hotpot is a Lancashire stew of meat topped with sliced potatoes, a traditional northern English dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lancashire hotpot is a slow-baked meat and potato casserole, a kind of stew.

clue.text: Are the house-proud likely to keep rubbing it in?

definitions.text: Are the house-proud likely to keep rubbing it in?

parts.words: Are the house-proud likely to keep rubbing it in?
parts.note: rubbing it in sounds like nagging, but tidy homeowners literally buff wax into their tables and chairs

explanation.definitionFit: Waxy cleaning product rubbed into tables and chairs to make the wood shine.

clue.text: Regret having one and ten in pennies!

indicators.note: the letters for one and ten sit inside the coins' word

parts.note: pence is the plural of penny
the Roman numeral I is one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sorry for spending small change on a coin collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitence is sorrow and contrition for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Taking the place of another minister with debts

parts.note: a vicar is a parish minister of the Church of England
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A substitute clergyman who owes money.
explanation.walkthrough: IOU stands for 'I owe you', a note promising repayment.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicarious means experienced or done in place of someone else, as a substitute.

clue.text: Not willingly late

parts.note: late here means deceased, and not willingly means without having made a legal will

explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies without leaving a valid will is described this way in law.

clue.text: A great number of soldiers

definitions.meaning: a multitude, as in 'their name is ...'
a Roman army division of several thousand troops

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a vast multitude and a large military unit, as in the Roman army.

clue.text: Transport in French trap rebuilt by the river

parts.note: the French word for in is en

indicators.note: a rebuilt trap has its letters put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A French pony-trap is reconstructed beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like the trap of the surface, but here it is a verb meaning to delight; 'rebuilt' turns TRAP into RAPT.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone emotionally is to fill them with delight, to ravish them.

clue.text: Talk foolishly about one robber in the main

indicators.note: the chattering word goes around the numeral, enclosing it

parts.note: to prate is to chatter foolishly
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A blustering thief rambles on.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the open sea, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea robber, one who plunders ships on the high seas.

clue.text: Most of the canal cutting through an old land

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the Caledonian Canal runs across the Scottish Highlands

explanation.surface: A canal slicing across an ancient country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting through' just describes the canal crossing Scotland; drop the last letter N of the canal's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia was the Roman name for Scotland, still used poetically.

clue.text: To stop in the Andes is terrific

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: Halting a climb in the Andes is a marvellous idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or refrain from an action.

clue.text: Seemingly reasonable it might make Bill pause

indicators.note: says the letters of the following words can be formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An argument convincing enough to make Bill stop and think.
explanation.definitionFit: Plausible means appearing believable or credible on the face of it.

clue.text: There are not strings attached W when he has a hand in

definitions.text: There are not strings attached W when he has a hand in

parts.words: There are not strings attached W when he has a hand in
parts.note: a glove-puppet operator works with his hand inside the figure instead of a marionette's strings

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who works a glove or string figure for a show.

clue.text: It is linked to offer personal protection

definitions.text: It is linked to offer personal protection

parts.words: It is linked to offer personal protection
parts.note: medieval armour made of interlocking metal rings protecting the wearer

explanation.definitionFit: Armour of interlocking iron rings worn by knights.

clue.text: Not right to singe a small cake

indicators.note: drops R, the abbreviation for right

parts.note: to singe is to burn slightly

explanation.surface: Advice not to scorch a little cake while baking.
explanation.definitionFit: A bun is a small sweet bread roll or cake.

clue.text: Start, not being at home, to ask earnestly

indicators.note: the words for at home are taken away from the word for start

parts.note: to begin is to start
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone out of the house is to plead urgently.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg is to implore or plead.

clue.text: Lousy egg can be brought up

indicators.note: in a down light, bringing up reads the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A rotten egg can be thrown up.
explanation.definitionFit: A nit is the egg of a louse, hence lousy.

clue.text: In trying circumstances it shows a sense of humour

definitions.text: In trying circumstances it shows a sense of humour

parts.words: In trying circumstances it shows a sense of humour
parts.note: trying is read as being tried by a judge, so the amusement happens during a trial

explanation.definitionFit: Merriment in a courtroom, noted in law reports when a judge or witness raises a smile.

clue.text: Receive expression of surprise, say, from an alien

indicators.note: signals a letter whose spoken name matches the exclamation

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise
ET is the alien of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: Hearing an astonished gasp from a visitor from space.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something is to obtain or be given it.

clue.text: French one quietly gives help that is outstanding

parts.note: un is French for one
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
aid is help

explanation.surface: A Frenchman discreetly offers excellent assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise, but it means still owed.
explanation.definitionFit: An outstanding bill is still due, not yet settled.

clue.text: One saying that it is an old Greek coin

definitions.meaning: a gold or silver coin of ancient Greece

explanation.definitionFit: Read as one who states, and also the name of an ancient Greek coin.

clue.text: Beat graduates at the beginning of August

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
MAs are Masters of Arts, graduates

explanation.surface: Students are thrashed as summer term ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Lammas Day, 1 August, is the old English harvest festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Lammas is the feast day falling on the first of August.

clue.text: Bird taken in by one goddess or another

indicators.note: the bird's word is placed inside the goddess's name

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin
a hen is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird is captured by one deity or a rival one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the definition: a second goddess beside Ate.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene, or Athena, is the Greek goddess of wisdom, a further deity.

clue.text: Against new lot giving voice

parts.note: contra is Latin for against

indicators.note: new signals the following word is made over in fresh order

explanation.surface: Opposing a fresh batch of offers made at an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is the lowest female singing voice.

clue.text: Early enough eventually

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both punctually and given long enough, finally.

clue.text: Diana's pet may suffer from it

definitions.text: Diana's pet may suffer from it

parts.note: Di is the short form of Diana, and Di's is her possessive
a pet is a fit of bad temper, a sulk

explanation.surface: A princess's pet dog might catch a disease.
explanation.walkthrough: Distemper is a viral disease of dogs; the clue also reads as Di's temper, a fit of pique.
explanation.definitionFit: Canine distemper is an infectious disease suffered by dogs and other animals.

clue.text: Whopper perhaps about a German chemist

indicators.note: the phrase is turned about, its opening word moved to the back

parts.note: a whopper is a big lie

explanation.surface: Someone tells a massive fib concerning a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: Justus von Liebig was a 19th-century German chemist; the first word of the two-word phrase moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Justus von Liebig founded organic and agricultural chemistry in Germany.

clue.text: Extraordinary riches he had nurtured

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the ordinary, so the letters fall in another order

parts.note: had shortens to 'd, as in he'd

explanation.surface: Unusual wealth that someone once possessed.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish is to care for lovingly and tend.
